observation_summary: The compiler fails to issue warnings for useless code when that code is embedded as a non-rightmost element within a comma-separated expression.
reasoning_summary: The bug occurs because the compiler's side-effect checker only evaluated the first element of a comma-separated expression for potential side effects. Consequently, any non-rightmost expressions containing no side effects were ignored by the checker, failing to trigger a warning for useless code. The fix involved refactoring the logic to correctly traverse and evaluate all elements within comma expressions, ensuring that any expression lacking side effects is properly flagged regardless of its position in the sequence.
